title: Caterpillar symbic tree basis conjecture
statement: Let $E$ be the ground set of matrix entries, and let $\mathcal{B}\subset E$ be a set of size $2n-1$. A **symbic tree** is a combinatorial object indexing a maximal cone in the tropical variety of rank-two symmetric matrices; a **caterpillar symbic tree** is a symbic tree whose branches are caterpillars, meaning that each branch contains only one cherry. **Caterpillar symbic tree basis conjecture.** The set $\mathcal{B}$ is a basis of the matroid of some symbic tree if and only if $\mathcal{B}$ is a basis of the matroid of some caterpillar symbic tree. This would reduce the determination of all bases in the relevant matroid to symbic trees with caterpillar branches; the preceding proposition establishes the analogous statement for the union of bases of the algebraic matroids, but the conjectured equivalence for each basis is not resolved here.
source_name: May Cai, Kisun Lee and Josephine Yu, “The Tropical Variety of Symmetric Rank 2 Matrices”, arXiv:2404.08121 (2025).
